facts.text: Burton is in southeastern Genesee County, and its township residents voted on May 16, 1972 to incorporate as a city.
Over the years, Burton changed from an agricultural community into a suburban community.
For about 20 years the Burton area was known as the Atherton settlement, after members of the Atherton family who settled on Thread Creek in 1835.
The City of Burton campus, including City Hall and the Veterans Memorial, is on South Center Road at Manor Drive, between East Bristol Road and Maple Avenue.
Kelly Lake Park, off Lapeer Road west of Genesee Road, has a walking trail, a fishing dock, pavilions, a boat launch, a beach area and a sledding hill.

For-Mar Nature Preserve and Arboretum, a Genesee County Parks property on North Genesee Road in Burton, has more than 7 miles of trails, gardens and an arboretum, with Kearsley Creek winding through the park.
The Burton Parks and Recreation Commission lists a City Christmas Decorating Contest and a Christmas Tree Lighting among its seasonal community events.
Courtland Center, an enclosed shopping mall that opened in 1968 as Eastland Mall, sits at East Court Street and Center Road in Burton.
The Bendle, Bentley and Atherton school districts are located entirely within the City of Burton.

christmas-light-installation.title: Burton Christmas Light Installers | Holiday Light Service
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Burton, MI Christmas lights installed for you: roofline, tree and shrub lighting designed for your home, serviced through the season and removed after.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Burton, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Roofline, tree and shrub lighting for Burton homes, handled from the first design conversation to takedown after the holidays.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Burton makes a contest of it. The city's Parks and Recreation Commission includes a City Christmas Decorating Contest on its list of seasonal events, which gives front yards something to aim for. If you plan to enter, or simply want the house that neighbors slow down for, the design matters more than the bulb count. We start with the roofline, choose the trees and shrubs that deserve attention and lay out a display that feels balanced rather than busy. Burton grew from an agricultural community into a suburban one, and no single template fits every house here, so each plan is drawn for that specific house. We install it, look after it through the season and take it down in the new year.
considerations: Decorating with the contest in mind

If you want your home in the running for the City Christmas Decorating Contest, think about the street view first. Clean rooflines, fully wrapped trees and a clear focal point tend to read better than scattered decorations, and we can build the design around that goal.

A single tall tree in the front yard can anchor an entire display. We follow the trunk and main limbs with tight, even spacing so the tree keeps its form after dark, and once the branches climb past sensible ladder height, the work moves to the bucket truck.

Most holiday lighting goes up between October and early December, and open dates thin out as the holidays draw closer. If you want the display up before the city's tree lighting or a family gathering, request your estimate early for the widest choice of dates.
faq: Do you install Christmas lights in Burton?

Yes. Burton sits squarely in our Genesee County service area. Request a free estimate online or call (248) 756-8915, and we will talk through the rooflines, trees and shrubs you want lit and how you want the display to look.
Can you design a display for the decorating contest?

We can design with the contest in mind, focusing on what shows well from the sidewalk and the road, like crisp rooflines, wrapped trees and lit shrubs. Contest rules and judging come from the city, so check the current details there before you plan around a deadline.
Can we add to the display in later seasons?

Yes. A display can start with the roofline and a few key trees, then grow as you see how it looks on your house. Each estimate spells out what is included, from design and installation to in-season service and takedown, so adding a tree or a row of shrubs is easy to plan.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Burton Commercial Holiday Lighting | Holiday Light Service
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Holiday lighting for Burton, MI shopping centers, retail, offices and HOA entrances. Building outlines, tree wraps and lamppost decor. Free estimates.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Burton, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Building outlines, frontage trees, lamppost decor and lit entrances for Burton retail, offices, subdivisions and managed properties.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Burton's retail map runs from the enclosed mall at East Court Street and Center Road, open since 1968, to freestanding stores and offices across the city. For all of them, holiday lighting does two jobs. It tells people the business is open and ready for the season, and it makes the property easy to spot after dark. That usually means bold building outlines, lit entrances, wrapped trees along the frontage and pole or lamppost decor where the fixtures allow. Rooflines and tall trees are worked from our bucket truck, and we manage the display from design through in-season service and takedown, so your staff can stay off the ladders.
considerations: A shopping center has a lot of frontage to cover. We concentrate the design where shoppers actually look: entrances, sign areas, frontage trees and the roofline facing the main road. Pole and lamppost decor can then carry the look across the parking lot.

A lit entrance tells residents they are home. For subdivisions and condo communities, we treat the sign, the trees beside it and the plantings as a single scene, then put the proposal in front of whoever approves it, whether that is the board or a management company.

Retail properties usually want the lights up before holiday shopping picks up. Since the install calendar spans October to early December, a shop or center aiming to be lit for the start of the shopping season should book while the most dates are open.
faq: Do you light shopping centers and retail properties in Burton?

Yes. We serve Burton shopping centers, freestanding shops, offices and managed properties. We design for the whole site, from rooflines and frontage trees to pole and lamppost decor, and scope it in a free estimate.
Can you add pole or lamppost decor?

Yes. Pole and lamppost decor is a strong way to carry a holiday look through a parking lot, plaza or entrance drive, and it ties the far corners of a property back to the building. We look at the existing fixtures and design decor that suits them.
Can you schedule installation around business hours?

Yes. Tell us when the store is busiest, when deliveries arrive and where customers park, and we will build the install plan around it. Lift work near entrances can be set for quieter hours. Mention any constraints when you request the estimate so they are part of the plan from the start.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Lighting in Burton, MI | Holiday Light Service
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Permanent, app-controlled roofline lighting in Burton, MI for holidays, school game nights and everyday accent light. Request your free estimate today.
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: One roofline installation, controlled from your phone, for Christmas, Halloween, game nights and a clean glow every other evening.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: The Bendle, Bentley and Atherton school districts all sit entirely inside Burton, which makes game night a natural use for permanent lighting. The lights go up along your roofline one time, and from then on the app does the work: your team's colors on a Friday night, orange and purple for Halloween, warm white for everyday accent lighting and a Christmas palette once December arrives. For homeowners who put real effort into the City Christmas Decorating Contest, a permanent roofline gives the display a clean foundation every year, with seasonal tree and shrub lighting layered on top. Placement follows the eaves and peaks you already have, so the lights look like part of the house.
considerations: Game nights, homecoming and graduation parties are easy to celebrate when the roofline changes from an app. Pick your team's colors for the week, then return to warm white or a holiday scene afterward, with no strands to hang or take down.

When the decorating contest comes around, the roofline, usually the hardest part of a display to reach, is already done. That frees the season's effort for the yard, where tree wraps and shrub lighting are installed and removed on the usual holiday schedule.

Because permanent lighting stays up, we pay close attention to where it runs and how visible it is when off. The aim is hardware you barely notice in daylight and a crisp outline after dark, with the layout settled before anything is installed.
faq: Do you install permanent lighting in Burton?

Yes. Permanent, app-controlled roofline lighting is available throughout Burton. Send a quote request or call (248) 756-8915, and we will set up a free estimate that covers the design, where the lighting runs and what is included.
Do I have to run it every night?

No. You decide when it runs: warm white every evening, school colors on game nights, a holiday scene in December or nothing at all when you prefer a dark roofline. There is no schedule you have to keep, and every change is made from your phone.
What does a permanent lighting estimate include?

It covers the design, the roofline sections to be lit, how the system is controlled and what is included with installation. The estimate is free and spells out the scope, so you can weigh permanent lighting against seasonal installation before deciding.
